statusText: Calm, wait-and-see conditions persist into the European late-morning ahead of today's 12:30 UTC Retail Sales / 14:00 UTC preliminary UMich data cluster. This run's WebSearch again returned the identical S&P 500 (~7,825.25) and Nasdaq 100 (~30,177.50) futures levels and ranges as the prior two runs -- now a third consecutive stale/cached print rather than a fresh intraday read, a genuine live-evidence limitation. VIX holds flat near 14.5-14.6. Iran-Oman talks on reopening the Strait of Hormuz remain unresolved: Iran's Supreme National Security Council continues to withhold reopening pending U.S. "corrected behavior" even as Oman-brokered route coordinates are reportedly agreed -- progress-in-talks, not a resolved discontinuity. Russia-Ukraine strikes continue (a Russian Gazprom refinery ~1,300km from the border was hit today) with no confirmed broader risk-asset transmission. Alpha Vantage remains fully rate-limited for a seventh consecutive run (TREASURY_YIELD retried once, both attempts returned an immediate rate_limit error), so this assessment again relies entirely on WebSearch; combined with the now-repeated stale futures snapshot, Confidence eases into the low band this run.
recommendation: Current action remains EA_ON. Continue monitoring through the late European morning and into the 12:30 UTC Retail Sales and 14:00 UTC preliminary UMich sentiment cluster; an upgrade to a higher Tail state still requires observed persistent one-way structure with failed pullbacks in the broad Nasdaq-100 complex itself, not the pending data cluster, the unresolved Hormuz talks, continuing Russia-Ukraine strikes, or this run's continued Alpha Vantage outage and repeated stale futures print.
headline: Nasdaq-100/S&P futures levels unchanged for a third straight run in WebSearch results (stale print, no fresh intraday structure confirmed); VIX flat near 14.5-14.6; Iran-Oman Hormuz talks remain unresolved despite reported progress on route coordinates; Russia-Ukraine strikes continue without confirmed market transmission; today's 12:30 UTC Retail Sales and 14:00 UTC preliminary UMich sentiment remain the session's main checkpoints; Alpha Vantage remains fully rate-limited for a seventh consecutive run, so Confidence eases into the low band.
body: About 40 minutes past the top of the hour, conditions remain calm into the European late morning, roughly one hour on from the prior run. This run's WebSearch results for S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 futures again returned the identical price levels and session range as the prior two runs (S&P futures last ~7,825.25, range 7,773.75-7,838.50; Nasdaq 100 futures ~30,177.50, range 30,124.25-30,232.00) -- now a third consecutive stale/cached snapshot rather than a fresh intraday print, a genuine live price-path limitation this run, distinct from asserting the structure itself. VIX holds flat near 14.5-14.6, essentially unchanged from the prior run. Treasury yields were not directly observable via Alpha Vantage this run; WebSearch indicates the 10-year continues to hold near its recent range (~4.65-4.66%, last reliably observed Thursday), consistent with prior runs and not indicating fresh repricing. On the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's Supreme National Security Council continues to withhold a full reopening pending U.S. "corrected behavior," even as Oman-brokered route coordinates are reportedly close to final agreement -- this remains progress-in-talks rather than a resolved discontinuity, consistent with the prior run's framing. On Ukraine-Russia, strikes continue on both sides (a Russian Gazprom oil refinery roughly 1,300km from the Ukrainian border was hit today per Ukraine's General Staff, and Zelenskyy warned this week that Russia is preparing for escalation rather than peace) but no confirmed broader risk-asset transmission was identified this run. No fresh, index-relevant semiconductor or megacap catalyst was identified: Nvidia coverage continues to point to its Aug 26 earnings as the next real catalyst, with no new company-specific news this hour. Alpha Vantage's free-tier daily quota remains exhausted for a seventh consecutive run -- the TREASURY_YIELD call was retried once and returned an immediate rate_limit error both times -- so, per the fallback protocol, this assessment again relies entirely on WebSearch for yields, oil, VIX, equities and price-path context. Combined with the now third-consecutive identical/stale futures print, evidence quality has degraded further this run, and Confidence moves into the low band (38, down from 40) to reflect that. Tail holds at 9% (still low; no persistent one-way structure evidence, and calm overnight/morning conditions are not themselves a Nasdaq-100 price-path signal) while Stress holds flat at 26%, unchanged from the prior run, on generic session-transition and modest pre-event positioning ahead of the Retail Sales/UMich cluster, which remains the main driver of the forecast Stress path higher into midday UTC before easing back through the afternoon and into the next Asia handover.

lookbackSummary: Tail held in the low band (9-18%) through the full prior 24 hours as the index ground to a fresh S&P 500 record above 7,800 on soft PPI; Stress ran elevated to high (up to 58%) around the Wednesday/Thursday CPI-PPI and AMAT-earnings window before easing back into the low-to-moderate band (23-29%) by Friday's European morning as the after-hours reaction stayed contained to the single name and no broader transmission was confirmed.
outlookSummary: Tail is projected to stay low (5-11%) through the next 24 hours; Stress is projected to build from the high-20s toward the upper-40s across the 12:30-14:00 UTC Retail Sales / UMich sentiment cluster and the US cash-open/power-hour window before easing back through the evening and into the quiet weekend handover, with no forecast slot currently implying an action change from EA_ON. Confidence is projected to stay in the low-to-medium-low band throughout, reflecting the continued Alpha Vantage outage and repeated stale futures print.

forecastDetail.comment: European mid-morning: this run's WebSearch again returned the identical S&P/Nasdaq futures levels and range as the prior two runs (S&P ~7,825.25, range 7,773.75-7,838.50; NQ ~30,177.50, range 30,124.25-30,232.00) -- now a third consecutive stale/cached print, not fresh structure. VIX flat 14.5-14.6, Brent little changed as Iran-Oman Hormuz talks remain unresolved (Iran still rejects the strait is open).

Late European morning holds calm ahead of the U.S. data cluster; no fresh Hormuz kinetic escalation or Ukraine-Russia transmission to markets identified this hour (continued Russia-Ukraine strikes reported, including a hit on a Russian refinery, but no broader risk-asset transmission confirmed).

Pre-Retail-Sales positioning builds modestly into midday UTC; Stress ticks higher on event anticipation while Tail stays anchored in the low band absent any observed persistent one-way structure in the Nasdaq-100 complex itself.

Final hour before the 12:30 UTC Retail Sales print; Stress continues to build on forecast dispersion and event positioning, consistent with treating pre-event anticipation as a Stress rather than Tail driver.

Retail Sales (12:30 UTC) prints within this hour, the session's first major checkpoint; Stress rises toward the elevated band on event/whipsaw risk around the release, while Tail requires an observed failed-pullback/persistent-extension reaction before it could follow, which is not yet asserted.

University of Michigan preliminary sentiment (14:00 UTC) prints within this hour on the heels of Retail Sales, keeping the window in event/whipsaw mode; Stress is projected to peak here before easing through the afternoon as the data cluster clears.
